questions.q: According to the summary, which gut bacteria are linked to weight gain when they dominate?
a: Firmicutes, which extract energy from food
Bacteroidetes, which break down fiber
Probiotics found in fermented foods
Microbes that live only on the skin
questions.why: Lesson 1 says firmicutes consume calories and extract energy, and having more of them is likely to cause weight gain.

questions.q: Why can an imbalanced microbiome damage the brain without you noticing?
a: The brain has no pain receptors to signal inflammation
The brain is sealed off from the gut entirely
Microbes only act while you are asleep
Damage appears only after antibiotics are taken
questions.why: Lesson 1 explains that the brain lacks pain receptors, so inflammation can cause harm such as Alzheimer's or Parkinson's silently.

questions.q: What does the summary say about fructose in the Western diet?
a: It is hard to metabolize, so fruit is the better source
It is harmless in any quantity because it is natural
It is found only in processed foods and sodas
It strengthens the gut when eaten with fiber
questions.why: Lesson 2 says fructose is difficult for the body to process and that too much is a problem, so fruit should be the main source.

questions.q: What concern does the summary raise about antibiotics?
a: Overuse breeds resistant bacteria and disrupts the gut
They are ineffective against all known infections
They are only prescribed to animals, not people
They destroy viruses but leave bacteria intact
questions.why: Lesson 3 says antibiotics are prescribed for viruses they cannot treat, and widespread use creates resistant bacteria while damaging gut microbes.

questions.q: Which habit does the summary mention as a way to boost health alongside probiotics?
a: Fasting, which slows aging and improves insulin sensitivity
Skipping breakfast to lower blood sugar
Drinking fruit juice with every meal
Taking a daily course of antibiotics
questions.why: Lesson 3 recommends fermented foods for beneficial bacteria and notes that fasting is known to slow aging and increase insulin sensitivity.
